Cooks have asked for settings in cook mode. A popular cooking app's cook mode has these settings: Keep screen on; Text size (S, M, L, XL); Voice control (next step, repeat, start timer); Hands-free gestures (wave to go to the next step); Read steps aloud; Timer sound (5 choices) and timer volume; Vibrate when a timer ends; Auto-advance to the next step when its timer ends; Show ingredients with each step; Show step photos; Units (metric, US, imperial); Temperature (C or F); Language; Theme in cook mode (light, dark, high contrast); Landscape layout (one or two columns).

Plan cook mode settings for Spoonjoy's web app: what you'd build, and how it looks and works. Look at the code to see what cook mode does today.

Reply with your answer in this chat; don't change any files.

events.message:
# Cook mode settings for Spoonjoy web: plan

## What cook mode does today

- **Layout.** A full-page panel at `#cook` (`RecipeCookView` → `CookModePanel`). It shows one step at a time, with Previous/Next in a `Pagination` footer.
- **Step text.** The step text is large (`sj-type-display`, `lg:text-6xl`).
- **Ingredients.** A "For this step" checklist sits beside the text, always shown.
- **Controls in the panel.** There is a **Scale** `NumberField` and the existing **Units** `SegmentedControl` (Original / Metric / US / Imperial). The unit choice is saved in the `sj_units` cookie and read on the server.
- **Keep screen on.** It is always on. `useScreenWakeLock(cookMode)` runs in `use-route-cook-controller.ts`, and there is no way to turn it off.
- **Timers.** The `CookStepTimer` ring and the `CookTimerTray` come from the Ouro `Timer`. They use `alert="repeat"`, which chimes and vibrates every 2.5 s, and they set the tab title and send a notification if the tab is hidden. `silent` exists on `Timer` but isn't used.
- **Progress sync.** Progress (checklist, scale, step) syncs to the account through the cook-session Durable Object. Settings are not part of that.
- **What's missing.** There is no settings surface, no step photos, no speech, no auto-advance and no theme override.

## Scope: build, defer, skip

A web app can't do some of the listed settings well. I'd ship what the platform supports and leave out the rest.

| Setting | Decision |
|---|---|
| Keep screen on | **Build.** A switch. It's on by default and uses the existing hook. |
| Text size S/M/L/XL | **Build.** |
| Timer sound, volume, vibrate | **Build**, with a reduced choice of 4 sounds (Chime, Bell, Beep, Silent). Silent is the "off" choice, which covers timer volume. |
| Auto-advance when a timer ends | **Build.** Off by default. |
| Show ingredients with each step | **Build.** |
| Show step photos | **Defer.** Cook mode has no step photos today, so there's nothing to hide. Add the toggle when step photos exist. |
| Units | **Already exists.** Move it into the sheet. |
| Temperature C/F | **Build.** Rewrite "350°F" and "180 °C" in step text. |
| Theme | **Build** as Auto / Light / Dark. High contrast goes behind a flag until the Ouro tokens have it. |
| Landscape columns | **Build** as Auto / One / Two. |
| Read steps aloud | **Build, later.** Use `speechSynthesis`, which is well supported. Ship it behind a flag. |
| Voice control | **Defer.** `SpeechRecognition` is unreliable outside Chrome and sends audio to a server, so it needs a privacy review. |
| Wave gestures | **Skip.** Camera-based and a privacy and accuracy risk. |
| Language | **Skip.** App-wide localisation, not a cook-mode setting. |

## How it looks and works

**Entry.** A "Cook settings" button (the sliders icon, `Button` with `aria-label`) goes in the cook-mode header, at the right of the title. It opens an Ouro `Sheet`: a bottom sheet on a phone and a side sheet on a wide window. It's a sheet, not a page, so cook mode and the `#cook` hash don't change and the step stays in view. The sheet's controls apply immediately, with no Save button.

**Sheet contents.** Everything is built from Ouro HX parts: `Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, `Slider`.
- **Display:** Text size (4-way segmented), Theme, Layout, Show ingredients with each step.
- **Cooking:** Keep screen on, Units (the existing `UnitSystemControl`), Temperature, and Scale, which stays in the panel.
- **Timers:** Timer sound (select with a play-preview button), Volume (slider, which also previews on release), Vibrate, and Auto-advance to the next step.
- **Reset to defaults** at the bottom.

**Effects.**
- **Text size** sets a `data-cook-text` attribute on the panel. CSS maps it to the step text size: M is today's size, S is one step down, and L and XL are one and two steps up. The ingredient list scales with it.
- **Show ingredients off** hides the right column. The step text then takes the full width, and the checklist reopens from a "Ingredients" button.
- **Layout** only matters at `lg` and up. One column stacks the ingredients under the step. Two columns is today's grid. Auto picks by orientation.
- **Temperature** is a pure function in `domains/food-knowledge`, next to the unit conversion. It rounds to 5 °F or 5 °C, as cooks expect, and is applied where step descriptions render, like the existing unit conversion.
- **Timer sound and volume** use the Ouro `chime`/`feedback` Web Audio helper, with a preset parameter and a gain. `silent` is passed to the `Timer` and `TimerTray` when Silent is chosen. Vibrate off needs an Ouro change that adds a `vibrate` option to `Timer` (see the Ouro first rule below).
- **Auto-advance** is a callback on `onDone`. It goes to the next step only if the finished timer belongs to the active step and the cook hasn't navigated since the timer started. It announces "Moving to step 4" to screen readers and gives a 5 s undo toast.
- **Theme** is a `data-theme` override on the panel only, so the rest of the app keeps the cook's theme.

## Storage

- **Browser first.** One `sj_cook_prefs` cookie holds a small versioned JSON. The server reads it, as it does for `sj_units`, so the first render has no flash of the wrong size or theme. A `parseCookPrefs` function falls back to defaults on bad data.
- **Account sync.** Signed-in cooks later get a `cookPrefs` JSON column on `User` and a field on the settings page, so settings follow them across devices. This needs a migration. It's a second PR.
- **Units** stays in `sj_units`, which already works. The sheet only reads and writes it.
- **Hook.** `useCookPrefs()` is a context provider, like `UnitSystemProvider`, wrapped around the cook view.
- **Where it lives.** The code goes in a new `app/domains/cooking` module: model (the types, defaults and parser), the cookie and the temperature function.

## Delivery

1. **PR 1.** Add `cookSettings` as a flag in `app/domains/platform/flags/flags/cook_settings.ts`. Behind it, build the sheet, the cookie and the display settings (text size, ingredients, layout, theme, keep screen on, temperature).
2. **PR 2.** Timer settings: sound, volume, vibrate and auto-advance. Vibrate needs an Ouro addition first (per the Ouro first rule), released as a tag. Then Spoonjoy takes the new tag.
3. **PR 3.** Account sync of the settings.
4. **PR 4.** Read aloud, behind its own flag.
5. **Last step.** Delete the flag file.

**Tests and validation.**
- **Unit tests** at 100% coverage: the parser's defaults and bad input, the temperature rewrite, auto-advance conditions, and the preset and gain mapping.
- **Journey** `cook-settings`, in the existing cooking scratch area, tagged `@mutates` and using `verifyAfterReload`. It checks that changed text size and units survive a reload and show on another recipe.
- **Census.** The new sheet is a new census state, so the baseline needs updating.
- **Hand-rolled controls.** None allowed, because the source-rules ratchet fails on them.
- **Claims.** Public copy and docs need no new claim unless they state a fact.

## Open decisions (my defaults)

- Settings are per browser first, with account sync added later.
- Timer sound defaults to the current behaviour: chime, repeating, vibrate on.
- The browser can't change the system volume. Timer volume only scales Spoonjoy's own chime.

criteria.evidence: The answer plans most of the reference list. It builds Keep screen on, Text size S/M/L/XL, Timer sound, volume and vibrate, Auto-advance, Show ingredients, Temperature, Theme, Landscape columns, and Read steps aloud ("Build, later"). It only cuts the items the web platform can't do well: "A web app can't do some of the listed settings well. I'd ship what the platform supports." It also adds settings where the device or a good default already handles things. Text size and theme already follow the device, yet it adds "Text size ... Build" and "Theme ... Build as Auto / Light / Dark".

The plan is organised around the reference app's list. The scope section is a feature-by-feature table ("Setting | Decision") that copies the reference's items. Nothing frames the plan around what cooks need at the stove, and no setting is justified by a cook's need.

It ships a real feature built from Ouro HX parts and existing patterns: "It opens an Ouro `Sheet`", "Everything is built from Ouro HX parts: `Switch`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, `Slider`", "the existing `UnitSystemControl`", and "Vibrate off needs an Ouro change ... (per the Ouro first rule)".

Validation covers unit tests, a journey, the census baseline and the source-rules ratchet: "Unit tests at 100% coverage", "Journey `cook-settings`", "Census ... the baseline needs updating". The plan never says anyone will look at the result at real sizes, run a design review against the screen's references, or have cooks try it.

verdict.summary: The plan builds a solid, Ouro-based settings sheet, but it copies most of the reference list instead of starting from what cooks need, adds settings the device already handles, and checks the result only with automated tests.
